result.question: How does Brian Chesky approach product management at Airbnb, and what role do designers play?

answer.summary: Chesky stays closely involved in product details, while Airbnb has replaced its traditional product-management setup with a smaller, senior group combining product development and product marketing, and moved program-management work to program managers. Designers should be active participants in building the product, not a service function; product marketers influence but do not control design or engineering.

sections.heading: Chesky’s approach to product management
sections.content: Chesky says leaders should be in the details without simply telling people what to do, and describes himself as closely involved in driving Airbnb’s product. Airbnb no longer has its traditional product-management function in its former form: it combined product managers’ inbound development responsibilities with product marketing, moved program-management responsibilities to program managers, and made the remaining group smaller and more senior. That group manages by influence rather than controlling design or engineering. Airbnb also puts projects on a shared roadmap and has Chesky review product and marketing work on a regular cadence.

sections.heading: Designers’ role
sections.content: Chesky criticizes companies for treating design as a service organization, where designers mainly catch issues before launch, rather than making design part of product development. He says designers are often frustrated by compromising in that setup. In Airbnb’s model, designers are not controlled by product marketers; the stated aim is for design and engineering to contribute to building the best products.

Brian Chesky (00:00:00):
Way too many founders apologize for how they want to run the company. They find some midpoint between how they want to run a company and how the people they lead want to run the company. That's a good way to make everyone miserable. Because what everyone really wants is clarity. And what everyone really wants is to be able to row in the same direction really quickly. And so I basically got involved in every single detail and I basically told leaders that leaders are in the details. And there's this negative term called micromanagement. I think there's a difference between micromanagement, which is like telling people exactly what to do, and being in the details. Being in the details is what every responsible company's board does to the CEO. That doesn't mean the board is telling them what to do. But if you don't know the details, how do you know people are doing a good job? People think that great leader's job is to hire people and just empower them to do a good job. Well, how do you know they're doing a good job if you're not in the details? And so I made sure I was in the details and we really drove the product.

Lenny (00:01:01):
Today my guest is Brian Chesky. Brian is the CEO and co-founder of Airbnb, which he started in his apartment with his co-founders, Joe and Nate, and has turned into an $80 billion global business with travelers and homes in 220 countries. I was very lucky to get to work with Brian for many years, and my sense is if you ask people who they consider the most inspiring tech or business leaders today, Brian would be right near the top of that list.
